record.paper_title: Global results on rational systems in the plane, part 1
record.context_brief: period-two trichotomy for planar rational systems
record.original_question: For the planar rational system x_{n+1} = (a + b x_n + g y_n)/(A + x_n), y_{n+1} = x_n, with nonnegative parameters and positive denominators, extend and generalize its period-two trichotomy to broader planar rational systems: when g < b + A every solution converges to a finite limit, when g = b + A every solution converges to a not necessarily prime period-two solution, and when g > b + A some initial conditions produce unbounded solutions. The problem is to identify analogous trichotomy statements and parameter regimes for rational systems in the plane.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2.5. Extend and generalize the period-two trichotomy result described by Corollary 2.1 to rational systems in the plane.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the planar rational difference system
\[
x_{n+1} = \frac{a + b\,x_n + g\,y_n}{A + x_n}, \qquad y_{n+1} = x_n, \qquad n = 0,1,2,\dots,
\]
where the parameters $a, b, g, A \ge 0$ are nonnegative real numbers and the initial conditions $(x_0, y_0)$ are chosen so that the denominator $A + x_n$ remains positive for all $n \ge 0$. For this system the following period-two trichotomy is known:

(i) if $g < b + A$, then every solution converges to a finite limit;
(ii) if $g = b + A$, then every solution converges to a (not necessarily prime) period-two solution;
(iii) if $g > b + A$, then there exist initial conditions producing unbounded solutions.

Problem. Identify a broad class of planar rational systems of the form
\[
x_{n+1} = \frac{\alpha_1 + \beta_1 x_n + \gamma_1 y_n}{A_1 + B_1 x_n + C_1 y_n}, \qquad y_{n+1} = \frac{\alpha_2 + \beta_2 x_n + \gamma_2 y_n}{A_2 + B_2 x_n + C_2 y_n},
\]
with nonnegative parameters and positive denominators along orbits, and formulate and prove an analogous period-two trichotomy: determine explicit conditions on the parameters under which (i) every solution converges to a finite limit, (ii) every solution converges to a period-two solution, and (iii) some solutions are unbounded, thereby extending and generalizing the trichotomy stated above.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem on extending a known period-two trichotomy to broader classes of planar rational systems. No comprehensive solution providing such a trichotomy for general planar rational systems was located; only partial results for specific subfamilies appear in the literature on competitive/rational planar maps.
